instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Chop 1 tbsp each of thyme, sage and rosemary and mix them in a small bowl with the salt and pepper.
Pat the turkey dry with paper towels and rub the herb mixture all over it.
Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add the turkey and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side, including the edges, until golden.

Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake for 20 to 23 minutes. You're cooking it to 160°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest part: it's done when there's no pink left.
Transfer the turkey to a cutting board and let it rest for 10 minutes. It will climb to about 165°F as it rests.

Meanwhile, put the skillet on the stove over medium-high heat. The handle will be hot, so use an oven mitt. Pour in the broth and scrape up the browned bits. Boil for about 5 minutes, until it has reduced by half. That should be about 1/2 cup.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Slice the turkey 1/2 inch thick, and spoon the pan sauce over it.
method_notes: Xoxobella is the lead (herb rub of thyme, sage and rosemary, a sear on each side, then an oven finish to 160°F and a rest), but it has only 2 ratings, so this is a fallback lead; no herb-roasted version with 20 or more ratings could be read. This Is How I Cook (1 rating) adds the idea of deglazing the pan with broth, which is used here instead of its butter to keep the dish dairy-free. The broth is listed as gluten-free, so check the label.
